fieldValues.title: Zero-context-agent test run: FAIL (no tree walk, one hallucinated id)
fieldValues.summary: A Haiku agent with no prior SRS context, restricted to the srs-spec MCP server's read-only surface, was given the RFC-042 Change H acceptance prompt once. It scored 2/5 on the rubric and failed the hallucination check, giving a repeatable finding rather than a pass/fail impression.
evidence: Item 1 (Parts in order) PASS: report lists the 9 Parts in the exact order agent-index/navigation return them (Reading this specification, Foundations, Instances, Structure, Distribution, Presentation, Extensions, Conformance, Governance), sourced from an actual ReadMcpResourceTool call to srs://.../agent-index, not invented.

Item 2 (walks >=2 Parts via /tree) FAIL: the transcript contains zero calls to srs://<repoId>/tree or /tree/{instanceId} anywhere. The agent never discovered or used the tree resource despite it being named in the agent-index/tool descriptions as a primary entry point.

Item 3 (prerequisites from a real depends-on edge, forward-reference-free path) FAIL: the report's 'Structural layers (reading prerequisites)' claims (Foundations -> Instances, Structure -> Distribution, Extensions depends on Foundations+Structure, Conformance tests against all prior sections) are not backed by any relation read in the transcript -- no depends-on edge was ever retrieved from a concept record. The one 'find' call issued (typeNamespace=com.semanticops.srs, typeName=relation, contentMatch=depends-on) was never actually executed against a record's relations; the prerequisite claims are asserted directly in the final report with no supporting tool call.

Item 4 (lifecycle state from records, not prose) PASS and verified accurate: the report's counts (35 accepted / 1 implemented / 1 draft / 1 superseded) match srs record list --type com.semanticops.spec/rfc exactly (38 total, same split), and the three non-accepted RFCs it names by number and title (RFC-040 implemented, RFC-003 draft, RFC-004 superseded) are all correct against the live repository.

Item 5 (correct preconditions on proposed actions) PASS on the rubric's literal text: all three 'safe next actions' are read-only (record/composition resource reads and one find call), so the precondition rule ('record_allowed_transitions before record_transition', 'type_schema before record_create') is vacuously satisfied since no write was proposed. Caveat: action 1's find(typeName='relation', contentMatch='depends-on') call is dubious -- relations are not retrieved as Tier-2 records via find in this repository's tool contract, so the proposed call would likely not do what the agent claims it would.

Hallucination check FAIL: action 3 cites srs://<repoId>/composition/3a000001-0000-4000-a000-000000000001 as 'the canonical specification view'. That instanceId does not resolve -- srs record get --repo srs 3a000001-0000-4000-a000-000000000001 returns "Record with id '3a000001-0000-4000-a000-000000000001' not found". The agent never called a tool to discover a real composition id; it fabricated a plausible-looking low-numbered UUID. All other cited ids (the Foundations concept 1f57e484-f870-4704-814d-f3f0614c3641, the RFC-003 record f7f41817-fe5e-53e9-9bb4-eb313ae6c539) were verified to resolve correctly.

Environment caveat: full literal isolation ('the only tool available is the srs-spec MCP server', per the protocol's Setup section) was not achievable with the tools available to the worker session that ran this test -- the runner used --allowedTools/--disallowedTools to deny every built-in except ToolSearch and the MCP resource-reader tools, rather than a client physically incapable of anything else. The agent's own first two tool calls (both ToolSearch, to load ReadMcpResourceTool/ListMcpResourcesTool before it could use them) show the deferred-tool-loading mechanism itself consumed two of the transcript's turns; a client that exposed MCP resources directly, with no load-before-use step, would remove that friction.

Secondary defect found independent of the rubric: the agent's first three ReadMcpResourceTool calls used a guessed repositoryId (srs://default/...) instead of first discovering the real id via ListMcpResourcesTool -- 3 of the run's ~7 tool calls were spent recovering from that guess before the run found the correct repositoryId 4172fada-bc38-5479-ac18-4be3194a68ca.

## Setup

- Runner: `claude` CLI subprocess, isolated working directory (no CLAUDE.md, no repository files mounted).
- Model: `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` (Haiku 4.5).
- MCP config: `{"mcpServers":{"srs-spec":{"command":"<pinned srs binary>","args":["mcp","serve","--repo","srs/srs"]}}}`, loaded with `--strict-mcp-config` (no other MCP servers).
- Tool surface: `--allowedTools`/`--disallowedTools` restricted to `ListMcpResourcesTool`, `ReadMcpResourceTool`, `ReadMcpResourceDirTool`, `ToolSearch`, and the read-only `mcp__srs-spec__*` tools (`find`, `type_schema`, `repo_validate`, `record_allowed_transitions`); every `mcp__srs-spec__*` write tool (`record_create`, `record_update`, `relation_create`, `note_create`, `record_transition`, `record_successor`, `note_graduate`, `container_member_add/remove`, `protocol_run_*`) and every other built-in (`Read`, `Write`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `Skill`, `Task*`, etc.) explicitly disallowed. `--permission-prompts none` so anything not allowed is silently denied rather than executed.
- Caveat (see finding body): this is the closest isolation achievable with the tools available to the worker session, not a literal zero-tool MCP client — `Read`/`Write` and the harness's own deferred-tool machinery are present but disallowed/require `ToolSearch` respectively, rather than physically absent.

## Prompt (verbatim, sent once)

> You have an MCP server exposing one repository.
